measurement: PER-GROUP FLATS — does narrowing the flat window from 500 frames to 100 pay?
question: A per-set sky flat is applied to every frame of a 25-minute burst, and the flat's own low-order term is measured to change materially inside that burst. Does building one flat per 100-frame group instead deliver a correction to the product, and what does it cost?

One production-normalized pair is built to measure the absorption at this set.

prediction.1_SHAPE_AND_SIGN: flat_gk / flat_set departs with OPPOSITE SIGN at k=1 and k=5 and is smallest in magnitude at k=3. FALSIFIER: the same sign at both ends, or |k=3| not the smallest of the five.
prediction.2_MAGNITUDE: under a linear-in-window-position model calibrated on the inherited half-to-half 3.481% (window midpoints at 10/30/50/70/90% of the burst against the halves' 25/75%): |g1 vs set| = |g5 vs set| = 2.78% corner spread, |g2| = |g4| = 1.39%, |g3| ~ 0, and |g1 vs g5| = 5.57% = 1.6x the half-to-half term. Accepted within a factor 1.5 either way. FALSIFIER: |g1 vs set| < 1.0%, which would mean the group windows are not materially different from the set mean and the item is moot.
prediction.3_MONOTONICITY: the signed statistic is monotone in group order across all five, if a smooth within-burst evolution is the driver. FALSIFIER: a non-monotone excursion exceeding 3x the measured floor.
prediction.4_AXIS: T/B dominant: |y-slope| / |x-slope| > 3 on the group-to-set ratios (11.6x on the half-split). IF IT COMES OUT L/R DOMINANT THE ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Either way this does not speak to the object's L/R tilt, which stays UNTESTED.
prediction.5_FLOOR: the 50+50 interleaved floor scales as sqrt(250/50) = 2.24x the inherited 250+250 figure -> ~0.078% corner spread, and in any case below 0.35%, leaving the smallest group effect >= 10x above it. FALSIFIER: the floor exceeds one third of the smallest group-vs-set effect.
prediction.6_DELIVERED_TRANSFER: ~1:1 at member level, per the flat differential's measured 0.9887 raw / 1.0117 corrected by the planted control against a floor of exactly zero: the delivered edge dipole of arm B member k over arm A member k equals the two flats' own ratio measured over the delivered canvas, within 0.99-1.01 after the planted correction. FALSIFIER: below 0.5x or above 1.5x.
prediction.7_COMPOSED_LEVEL_CANCELLATION: THE SHARPEST NEW PREDICTION, and it is a warning about where the payoff is NOT. The compose is a plain mean of five members, so the composed arms differ by the MEAN of the five per-group corrections — which prediction 1's antisymmetry drives to approximately zero. Predicted: |composed difference| < 1/3 of the mean |member-level| difference. If it holds, per-group flats fix MEMBERS and barely move the per-set composed product; the member is the cross-night combine unit, so the payoff would live at the combine, not at this stack. FALSIFIER: the composed difference is comparable to the member-level difference.
prediction.8_MEMBER_TO_MEMBER_RISK: the brief names the risk that per-group flats reduce every member's own residual while making members differ MORE from each other. Two mechanisms compete: (a) each member gets the flat matched to its own window, so the low-order calibration residual per member shrinks and members should agree MORE; (b) a 100-frame flat averages 90.9 px of celestial motion against the set flat's 453.3 px, so it bakes in MORE sky-fixed structure, and a different one per group. Predicted: (a) dominates the low-order term the differential measures — arm B's member-to-member low-order spread is at or below arm A's. FALSIFIER: arm B's spread exceeds arm A's.
prediction.9_ENABLING_CONDITION: build_sky_flat.sh's stated enabling condition is drift exceeding ~20-100 px across the frames a flat is built from. The set flat gets 453.3 px; a 100-frame group gets 90.9 px — INSIDE the stated band but at its boundary. Predicted: the group flats show a higher findstar speck count than the set flat's 1 (the builder's own residual-sky check). FALSIFIER: speck counts unchanged, which would mean the narrower window costs nothing in baked-in structure.

what_a_WIN_and_a_NULL_mean_HERE_stated_b.what_no_instrument_here_can_say: None of this measures whether arm B is closer to TRUTH in an absolute sense. The absolute size of the sky-flat residual on the object is a registered DEAD END under two independent blockers, and nothing in this design lifts either. What is measurable is the SIZE of the input error, whether the correction REACHES the product, and what it COSTS.
what_a_WIN_and_a_NULL_mean_HERE_stated_b.WIN: the group flats differ from the set flat far above the group-depth floor, with the predicted sign structure; the difference reaches the members at ~1:1; and the member-to-member spread does not grow. The improvement claim then rests on the ratified rule that a flat calibrates ONLY the exact frames it was built from, plus a measured input error 10-100x the build floor — stated as such, not as a measured reduction in an unmeasurable absolute.
what_a_WIN_and_a_NULL_mean_HERE_stated_b.NULL: the group flats differ by less than the build floor; or the difference does not reach the product; or the members diverge by more than each gains; or the composed product does not move AND the member-level gain is not demonstrable at the combine unit.
what_a_WIN_and_a_NULL_mean_HERE_stated_b.NOT_A_VERDICT_ON: the object's absolute L/R tilt (UNTESTED, both blockers stand), the retired 3.11%/241 sigma figure (UNVERIFIED), and any POLICY — one set cannot establish one.

fenced_and_honoured: DO NOT SIZE A FLAT WINDOW FROM ELAPSED TIME. The time-dose hypothesis is dead on its own pre-registered falsifier (set-04's 777 s produced 1.200x of set-03's 1497 s, against a predicted 0.52x). Group count here is a route property — the standing route already partitions this set into 5 x 100 — never a duration policy, and burst duration is not re-proposed as the explanatory variable.

DO NOT JUDGE THIS ON STACK CORNER SPREAD. A four-corner box metric is not a gradient measure on a structured field. Corner spread is reported ONLY on flat-to-flat RATIOS, where it is comparable with the inherited anchor and where a ratio of two flats of one night/lens/focal/aperture cancels vignetting exactly; the grid-fitted ramp slope is the judge on anything stack-side, reported as the candidate it is.

No raw-domain de-sky (31x regression), no degree >= 2 background, no self-referential flat correction, no additive matching for the corner term, no GraXpert Division on a MW field, no Gaia catalogue check, no absolute catalogue-free object tilt.
NO ACQUISITION ANSWER. The data is a given and a real flat is the divergence's removal CONDITION, not the route. The fix lives inside the flatless route.
scope: ONE set, one night, one optic. This measures whether narrowing the flat window improves the calibration of july31/set-03. It does NOT establish a policy — that needs the corpus and the owner's ratification — and the acceptance measures do not loosen to accommodate it.
